Early accounts state Taylor was shot five times, one shot being deflected by his pocket watch. Later analysis suggests the watch would have all but disintegrated if struck by a bullet and that the damage to the watch face likely happened when Taylor collapsed on the windowsill, causing the watch pin to pierce the face from the inside. See Glen M. Leonard,Nauvoo: A Place of Peace, a People of Promise(Salt Lake City: Deseret Book, 2002), 397.

Many have assumed that Taylor, who was editor of the newspapers, authored the account, though he was still convalescing from his wounds at the time it was written. W. W. Phelps and others may have helped write section 135, relying in part on the eyewitness testimonies of Taylor and Richards. See Jeffrey D. Mahas, “Remembering the Martyrdom:D&C 135,” in Matthew McBride and James Goldberg, eds.,Revelations in Context: The Stories behind the Sections of the Doctrine and Covenants(2016), 304–5.
